item.title: [New] October 2026 security updates: 174 Critical CVEs, among them AD DS and Exchange Server remote code execution and an AD FS spoofing flaw
item.description:
Three of the Critical fixes sit on tier-0 hosts — domain controllers, AD FS and NDES — where a remote code execution is a forest compromise.

Windows · Patch domain controllers, AD FS, NDES and Exchange servers first, verify the October build on each with Defender Vulnerability Management, and keep the AD FS DKM hardening (MC1471963) enforcement in mind when testing AD FS.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 gets its last security update in January 2027 (90-day reminder)
item.description:
LTSC builds sit on kiosks, OT and lab machines that are rarely re-imaged; after January they stop receiving fixes unless covered by ESU.

Windows · Find LTSC 2021 devices in Intune or MDE device inventory (OSVersion 10.0.19044 with an LTSC SKU) and plan upgrade to LTSC 2024 or ESU enrollment.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Windows Server 2016 gets its last security update in January 2027 (90-day reminder); Essentials features end the same day
item.description:
Domain controllers, AD FS, Exchange and CA servers on 2016 stop receiving security fixes in 89 days unless they are on ESU; the first post-January vulnerability in Kerberos or Netlogon would be unpatched on them.

Windows Server · List every Windows Server 2016 host by role (DC, AD FS, CA, Entra Connect, Exchange), decide per host between upgrade to 2025 and an ESU purchase, and start with tier-0 roles.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Windows Server 2022 left mainstream support on 13 October; security updates continue to 14 October 2031
item.description:
Security fixes continue, but non-security fixes and feature work stop; a defect found on a 2022 domain controller or AD FS host from now on is fixed only if it is a security issue.

Windows Server · Record Windows Server 2022 as extended-support in the asset inventory and put 2022 domain controllers and tier-0 hosts on the Windows Server 2025 upgrade plan; nothing breaks today.

item.title: [New] October Patch Tuesday fixes an exploited Windows Shell security feature bypass (CVE-2026-96951, CVSS 8.8)
item.description:
An exploited shell bypass typically defeats Mark-of-the-Web or SmartScreen prompts on a downloaded file, which is how phishing payloads reach execution; every unpatched workstation is exposed.

Windows · Prioritise the October cumulative update on end-user devices, confirm coverage in Defender Vulnerability Management by CVE ID, and hunt for files launched from Downloads or archive paths on unpatched hosts.

item.title: [New] Windows 11 security baselines turn Administrator protection on by default from the October update
item.description:
Administrator protection replaces the admin's standing elevated token with just-in-time elevation through a separate system-managed account, which changes how local-admin elevation appears in endpoint telemetry and can break scripts and tools that expect silent elevation.

Windows · Test the baseline on a pilot ring, decide the two UAC policies explicitly in Intune or Group Policy, and re-baseline any detections keyed on elevation events.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] ReFS on removable media: audit from the October update, blocking by default from the January 2027 update
item.description:
Removable-media ReFS is an unsupported parsing surface; the audit events are new endpoint telemetry worth collecting, and the January default will block any workflow still relying on it.

Windows · Collect the new ReFS audit events, find workflows that depend on ReFS removable media, and test blocking before January.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.description:

Windows Server · After patching, check the AD FS Admin log for Event ID 1132 on every federation server and remediate Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 by hand.

item.title: [New] Windows 11 26H2 security baseline is reissued as v2: Administrator protection is now part of it, with credential prompts on the secure desktop
item.description:
Administrator protection replaces the split-token admin session with a separate, just-in-time elevation that asks for credentials. A baseline that enables it changes how every local-admin elevation looks in the logs and breaks tools that relied on silent elevation.

Windows · Take the v2 package from the Security Compliance Toolkit, test Administrator protection on admin workstations first, and brief the help desk on the new credential prompt.
